gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the P1S's internal 24 V supply is only 108 W and powers everything except the heated bed, which runs straight off the mains. A line flicker or sag therefore reboots the printer through that small supply, and the CyberPower datasheet says its AVR fixes low-voltage sags 'without switching to battery mode'. A forum owner reported P1S printers freezing mid-print during brownouts on an EcoFlow DELTA 2 used as a UPS.
standout_why: I compared this against the cited forum thread 41205 (Power Interruption Alert), the cited thread 91609 (P1S mid-print power loss) and the P1S spec PDF that ChatGPT cited. In 41205, holmes4 says only that 'the bed draws directly from line voltage', which is part of the finding. None of the cited pages names the 108 W internal supply, separates a brownout from a full outage, or reports how a power station behaved in a sag. In 41205, post 5 asks whether a 20 ms transfer is acceptable and gets no answer. In 91609, no one reports a transfer time or names the printer's supply. The DELTA 2 brownout report sits in an uncited result from the second chat (forum 56939/4), and ChatGPT did not pass it on in any of the three answers.
decides: It confirms a line-interactive sine-wave UPS with AVR, such as the CyberPower CP1500PFCLCD, as the pick for flickers. Most flickers are sags rather than full outages, and the AVR raises low voltage without a battery transfer, so the printer's 108 W electronics supply never sees a gap. For long outages, a power station can still go behind or alongside the UPS, but the page should not promise that a power station's UPS mode keeps a P1S running through brownouts, because a P1S owner's DELTA 2 did not. Bed sizing on 120 V stays at the 350 W peak.

findings.label: Internal power supply rating and what it powers
findings.value: 24 V, 108 W, input 100–240 V; 'It powers all systems except the heated bed.' Part no. FAC059
findings.source_title: Bambu Lab Internal Power Supply (24V 108W), P1P, P1S, X1, X1C – 3DJake
findings.note: This is a reseller's listing of Bambu's spare part, with compatibility given as P1P, P1S, X1 and X1C. The printer's electronics, motors, hotend and controller run through this supply, so its hold-up time decides whether a millisecond transfer causes a reboot.

findings.label: Heated bed is fed from the mains, not the PSU
findings.value: Bed draws line voltage directly; on 120 V startup 'tops out at around 350' W, and printing settles at 100–130 W
findings.source_title: Power Interruption Alert! - Which UPS for a P1S+AMS? - Bambu Lab Community Forum
findings.note: These are figures from forum user holmes4 on 120 V. A fixed resistive bed on mains explains why the bed's draw is about 1,000 W at 220–240 V but about 350 W at 120 V.

findings.product: Bambu Lab X1C (same bed design as P1 series)
findings.label: Bed on mains, switched by contactor
findings.value: 'The heatbed does not run through a power supply' (mugglesmuggle); the contactor 'is switched on off 3 times in about 1~1.5 sec' at print start (Jelbert)
findings.source_title: Powersuply glitches on the net at start print - Bambu Lab Community Forum
findings.note: These are community posts with no Bambu staff reply. They support the split-power design: a mains bed plus a small DC supply.

findings.label: Owner report: UPS mode during brownouts with P1S printers
findings.value: 'doesn't reliably function as a UPS for 3D printers'; in brownouts two printers stopped mid-print with heads and beds frozen, and resuming after a restart left large print defects
findings.source_title: Is Ecoflow Delta 2 worth the money? - Bambu Lab Community Forum
findings.note: designrama ran three P1S printers (opening post, 2024-02-09), posted an update on 2024-10-17 and later wrote 'My Delta2 died'. The same user had written in March 2024 that the switch 'doesn't interrupt the printers at all'. On the same thread, MZip reports that an X1C on a DELTA Pro kept printing through storms. This is user evidence with no measured transfer times.

findings.label: AVR handles sags without a battery transfer
findings.value: 'AVR increases the AC power and maintains a safe voltage level without switching to battery mode'; line-interactive; 1,500 VA / 1,000 W; 3-year warranty including the battery
findings.note: This is the maker's datasheet. Because a sag is corrected on the transformer instead of by a battery transfer, the P1S's 108 W supply does not face a switchover gap during brownouts.
